claims.text: The AWSx ELB component provides APIs for provisioning Application and Network Load Balancers and integrates with API Gateway, ECS, Lambda, and VPC.
Targeting an EC2 instance with an ELB requires opening ingress traffic to the load balancer, which is explicitly needed for NLB but not for ALB.
ALBs automatically open ingress traffic to the ports they listen on, whereas NLBs do not.
HTTP/2 is not supported for NLBs; enableHttp2 enables it on ALBs.
The Pulumi AWS registry has API docs for ec2 LaunchTemplate and autoscaling Group at the linked paths.
In AWSx, passing the load balancer's target group in a task definition's portMappings causes AWSx to populate the ECS service's load balancer configuration automatically.
The AWSx ECS component (awsx.ecs classes) automatically creates the right ingress and egress rules; raw aws.ecs requires manual security group management.
The example ECS program exports a stack output named `url` used with curl.
ALBs offer two features making them more attractive for ECS than NLBs: dynamic host port mapping and path-based routing with priority rules.
Pulumi recommends ALBs for ECS services unless a service requires a feature only available with NLBs.
By default, an AWSx load balancer is created as internet-facing, using the VPC's public subnets.
AWSx load balancers accept either a `subnets` property (subnet objects) or a `subnetIds` property (subnet IDs) for an explicit list of subnets.
NLB listeners support protocols TCP, TLS, UDP, TCP_UDP, QUIC, and TCP_QUIC, while ALBs support HTTP and HTTPS; NLBs default to TCP and ALBs choose HTTP or HTTPS based on port.
AWS docs pages rule-action-types.html (fixed-response-actions and redirect-actions anchors) and listener-rules.html exist at the linked URLs.
The deregistrationDelay range is 0–3600 seconds with a default of 300.
The slowStart range is 30–900 seconds or 0 to disable, and it is disabled by default.
Target group stickiness is available for ALBs only.
targetType possible values are instance, ip, lambda, and alb, defaulting to instance; IP targets must be within the VPC's private subnet range, RFC 1918 ranges, or RFC 6598 range (100.64.0.0/10).
Health check interval range is 5–300 seconds with a default of 30 seconds.
healthyThreshold range is 2–10 with default 3.
unhealthyThreshold range is 2–10 with default 3, and for NLBs must equal healthyThreshold.
Health check timeout range is 2–120 seconds; AWS default is 6 seconds for HTTP target groups and 10 seconds for HTTPS, TCP, and TLS target groups.
